answer.evidence: The top of the building is a large green roof or awning. Rows 4-30 are its tile stripes, with a dark stripe line every 7 rows (rows 11, 18, 25). A lighter front-edge line sits at row 30, followed by dark eave shadow in rows 31-33. Below it is a south-facing wooden facade of about 46 rows (34-79) with three ticket windows, posts and a counter that has its own light top band at rows 62-65. The name sign is decor. The ATMs are plain vertical faces, but they are small next to the main body.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tidy, readable ticket office, but it is shallower than the references. Its green roof is built from only about 3 greens (a light top band, a mid body, a dark lower edge) with no per-tile scallops or highlights, so it reads as a flat slab. The walls and wood trim use 2-3 browns with little grain. The measured facts agree: 8 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 17% near-flat coverage against 0% for both. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown or green and are not a black sticker line. Detail is concentrated in the windows and the sign, while the roof and wall fields stay plain. Next to the richly textured tile roofs and speckled plaster of the references it looks thinner and flatter. When in doubt, fail.
